# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I am the Blind monkey. I can touch the bomb but cannot see colors or read text. My current tactile input is limited to a raised Braille character 'ꖜ' on the plate and unknown states for wires/display/light.

The Deaf monkey can see the bomb (colors, markings) but cannot hear or touch.
The Mute monkey can read the manual but cannot speak or touch.

Since I cannot see the visual state of the wires (color/cut status) or the display, and the Deaf monkey cannot feel the Braille or know if I've cut anything yet without seeing it, we have an information gap. However, the Deaf monkey *can* see the physical state of the wires. If I act blindly, I might cut the wrong one.

I need to establish communication. The Deaf monkey sees everything visually except what is purely tactile (like the Braille dot pattern depth, though they might see the dots). The Mute monkey has the manual.

Strategy:
1. I should signal to the Deaf monkey that I am ready to receive instructions based on what they see. Since I can't hear, I must gesture. But wait, the rules say "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." And "Deaf... Cannot Hear anything". So gestures are the only way to communicate *to* Deaf from me? No, Deaf can *see* gestures.
2. Actually, I need to know which wire to cut. Only Deaf can see the colors/wire types clearly enough to match with the Manual (which Mute reads).
3. I don't know what the Manual says. Mute doesn't know what the Bomb looks like. Deaf knows what the Bomb looks like but doesn't know the Manual.
4. This requires a relay. Mute -> Deaf (via speech? No, Deaf can't hear. Mute can't speak.)
   - Mute can read the manual. Mute can gesture. Deaf can see gestures.
   - So Mute can tell Deaf the rules via gestures.
   - Deaf can see the bomb. Deaf can gesture back to Mute? Or Deaf can gesture to Me (Blind)?
   - I (Blind) can gesture. Deaf can see my gestures.
   - I (Blind) can speak. Mute can hear/read my speech.

Let's trace the channels:
- **Me (Blind)**: Can Speak (Mute hears), Can Gesture (Deaf/Mute see). Can Act.
- **Deaf**: Can See (Bomb/Gestures). Cannot Hear. Cannot Touch.
- **Mute**: Can Read (Manual). Can Hear (Speech). Can See (Gestures). Cannot Speak. Cannot Touch.

Flow:
1. Mute reads manual. Mute gestures rules to Deaf.
2. Deaf sees bomb + understands rules from Mute.
3. Deaf needs to tell me which wire to cut. Deaf cannot speak. Deaf cannot touch. Deaf can only... wait. Deaf cannot send messages?
   - "Whoever can see receives your words; whoever can see receives the gestures you made."
   - "A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was."
   - Deaf CAN see. So Deaf receives gestures FROM others.
   - Can Deaf SEND? The prompt doesn't explicitly list Deaf's output channels in the same table format for *sending*, but usually, monkeys can perform actions available to them.
   - Table: Deaf | Can See... | Cannot Hear, or touch...
   - It doesn't say Deaf cannot speak or gesture. But Deaf is "Deaf", implying hearing impairment. Usually, in these puzzles, Deaf communicates via sign language (gestures).
   - Let's assume Deaf can gesture. If Deaf gestures, I (Blind) cannot see. Mute can see.
   - So Deaf -> Mute (Gesture) -> ??? Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture.
   - This seems like a bottleneck.

Alternative interpretation:
Maybe I should just ask Mute for help?
I can speak to Mute. "What does the manual say?"
Mute can read the manual. Mute can gesture to me? No, I'm blind. I can't see gestures.
Mute can speak? No, Mute is Mute.

So:
- I (Blind) can talk to Mute.
- Mute can read manual.
- Mute can gesture to Deaf.
- Deaf can see bomb.
- Deaf can gesture to... whom? If Deaf gestures, I (Blind) can't see. Mute can see.

- But Mute cannot tell ME what to do because Mute cannot speak and I cannot see.

Wait, look at the "VIEWABLE CONTEXT". It's empty.

PLATE engraved [ꖜ]. This is Braille. I can read this. ꖜ is Braille for... let's check standard Braille.
⠚ ⠅ ⠃ ⠝ ⠑ ⠞ ...
Braille char `ꖜ` (U+289C) is dots 1-2-3-4-5-6? No.
Unicode Braille Patterns:
`ꖜ` is U+289C.
Binary: 0x289C = 0010 1000 1001 1100.
Braille cell bits:
Dot 1 (0x01), Dot 2 (0x02), Dot 3 (0x04), Dot 4 (0x08), Dot 5 (0x10), Dot 6 (0x20), Dot 7 (0x40), Dot 8 (0x80).
Standard 6-dot Braille uses lower byte.
U+2800 + value.
Value = 0x9C = 156.
156 in binary: 1001 1100.
Bits:
Bit 0 (Dot 1): 0
Bit 1 (Dot 2): 0
Bit 2 (Dot 3): 1 (4)
Bit 3 (Dot 4): 1 (8)
Bit 4 (Dot 5): 1 (16)
Bit 5 (Dot 6): 0
Bit 6 (Dot 7): 0
Bit 7 (Dot 8): 1 (128) -- Wait, 156 is 128+16+8+4.
So Dots 3, 4, 5, 8? Or maybe just 3,4,5 if it's 6-dot?
If 6-dot, max is 63. 156 > 63. So it's an 8-dot Braille character.
Dots lit: 3, 4, 5, 8.
This might be a code key.

However, I don't have the manual content.

Let's reconsider the communication loop.
If Deaf cannot communicate directly to me, and Mute cannot communicate directly to me, I am isolated regarding instructions unless I can deduce them myself or if the other two can coordinate to influence me physically? No, I'm the only one who can touch.

`ꖜ` (Dots 3,4,5,8).

I will speak to Mute, asking for clarification on the manual, hoping Mute can convey it to Deaf, and Deaf can convey it to me?

But Deaf doesn't know the rules (Manual).
Mute knows the rules. Mute can gesture to Deaf.

1. Mute reads manual. Mute gestures meaning to Deaf.

Given the ambiguity, I should test this hypothesis.
I will start by signaling readiness.

However, Turn 1 context is empty. I haven't sent anything yet.

If I speak to Mute: "What is the rule for cutting wires?"
Mute can read the manual. Mute can gesture to Deaf.
Deaf can see the bomb.
If Deaf can speak, Deaf answers me next turn.

If Deaf CANNOT speak, we are stuck unless the Braille `ꖜ` is self-explanatory.

Let's assume Deaf CAN speak. It's the most logical path for a 3-person puzzle where one is blind and one is mute. The third (Deaf) is often the visual observer who can vocalize descriptions.

Action: I will speak to Mute to ask about the manual's contents regarding the wires, specifically looking for a color-to-wire mapping or a condition. I will also gesture to Deaf to acknowledge their presence and request visual confirmation if they can speak.

Actually, simpler: Just ask Mute what the manual says about the wires. Mute will process it. Next turn, hopefully Deaf speaks the solution.

One more thing: The Braille `ꖜ`.
If I cut a wire, I need to know WHICH one.
Wires are 1, 2, 3.
Positions are likely left-to-right or top-to-bottom. As Blind, I feel them. I need to map "Wire 1" to a physical location.

Plan:

2. Gesture to Deaf: "Describe the wire positions/colors." (Using symbols ✋ 👆 etc to indicate pointing/describing).

To Deaf: I want them to point out the wires.
Symbols: `👉` (point right), `👈` (point left), `☝` (index up).
Maybe `✋` (stop/wait) then `👉`?

And `☝` for "Top"?

Let's stick to simple directional cues. `👈` `👉` to ask about side wires.

Message to Mute: "What are the wire rules?"

```
speak(to="mute", text="What are the rules for cutting the three wires?")

```
